title: Gazpacho
subtitle: Andalusian chilled tomato and vegetable soup
excerpt: The cold soup of Andalusia: very ripe tomatoes blended with cucumber, red pepper, garlic, stale bread, olive oil, and sherry vinegar into a smooth, deeply refreshing cold soup that is the taste of southern Spain in summer.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gazpacho is the cold vegetable soup of Andalusia, the southernmost region of Spain, with ancient roots in the practice of pounding stale bread with water, olive oil, garlic, and vinegar to produce the ajo blanco (white garlic soup) from which the tomato-based gazpacho developed after tomatoes arrived in Spain from the Americas in the sixteenth century. It is a summer staple across southern Spain, consumed in huge quantities in homes, bars, and restaurants from June to September. The quality of the tomatoes is everything: gazpacho made with out-of-season tomatoes is disappointing. In summer, use the ripest, most flavourful tomatoes available. The bread provides body and binds the emulsion; it is traditional and should not be omitted.

content.text: Use the ripest possible tomatoes. The soup must be well chilled before serving: make it at least 4 hours ahead, ideally the day before, and taste after chilling since flavours change when cold. Season assertively; cold soup needs more salt than warm soup. Strain through a sieve if you want a smooth, restaurant-style result; a blender alone leaves small bits of skin and seeds.

items.preparation: very ripe; roughly chopped; cores removed
peeled, deseeded, roughly chopped; about 250 g
stale white bread, crusts removed; soaked in water for 5 minutes then squeezed out

content.text: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, red pepper, garlic, and soaked bread in a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Add the olive oil and sherry vinegar and blend again.

Pass through a fine sieve, pressing with a spoon to push through all the juice and flesh; discard the skins and seeds. Season generously with salt and pepper. Taste: the soup should be tangy, very savoury, and heavily tomatoey. Adjust the vinegar, salt, and olive oil.

Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until very cold. Taste again and adjust the seasoning before serving (cold dulls saltiness). Serve in bowls or glasses with a drizzle of olive oil and optional garnishes of finely diced tomato, cucumber, and croutons.
